e: The Supreme Court directs the government and the IDF to disclose a timeframe for the return of Palestinians displaced in the northern section of the West Bank.
A Hezbollah unexploded munition detonation in the Ramim Ridge region kills one child and injures 24 others, including schoolchildren and teachers.
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and Albanian Foreign Minister Ferit Hoxha sign an enlarged government-to-government cooperation agreement.

The Yesha Council announces that Defense Minister Israel Katz has ordered a ban on pro-Palestinian activists, whether Israeli or foreign, seeking to assist Palestinian olive growers in the West Bank during the harvest season, citing the Council's demand to prevent activists from "coming to the olive harvest area to create provocations and confrontations."
Israel participates in the Marrakech Airshow in Morocco for the first time since the Abraham Accords.
Following the IDF's recommendation, Defense Minister Israel Katz announces that crossings into the West Bank and Gaza will be closed during the days marking the 7 October attacks.

After the Flydubai Flight 1073 incident, the Israeli government admits that it does not independently vet foreign pilots. Prime Minister Netanyahu orders "a through review" of security procedures for international flights to Israel.
One person is killed and another individual is wounded after a small aircraft crashes along Route 65, in the vicinity of Kafr Qara.
The Supreme Court overturns the Central Election Committee's ban on Arab parties running for the 2026 Israeli legislative election.
A group of Israelis are rescued from Lalibela following days of being stuck due to fighting in Tigray.
Prime Minister Netanyahu announces new security measures in response to the Flydubai Flight 1073.
An Israeli airstrike kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Al-Qassam Brigades in northern Gaza.

Likud announces that Prime Minister Netanyahu has sued media outlets Haaretz, Yedioth Ahronoth, Channel 12, and journalists Shlomi Eldar, Uri Misgav, Nadav Eyal, Barak Ravid, and Attila Somfalvi, among others, for NIS 2.6 million ($850,000) over recent reports that he received warnings from UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed and Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel before the 7 October attacks.
The IDF announces that it prevented an attempt to transfer munitions from Jordan to Israel with a drone.
Defense Minister Israel Katz announces a "general closure" on the West Bank following a recommendation from the IDF, preventing Palestinian laborers from entering settlements amidst Sukkot.
Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announces that Israel will revoke diplomatic privileges and Israel-issued credentials of Dutch diplomats in Ramallah due to a settlement trade ban.

Prime Minister Netanyahu orders the drafting of an ICC case against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, citing Turkey's alleged persecution of Kurdish minorities and the Turkish government's alleged financial assistance for Hamas.
Sixty-one additional firms are added to an UN Human Rights Council list of firms which operate in Israeli West Bank settlements.

The Beersheba District Court adds 7.5 years to a man's prison sentence for using his role as a volunteer car-tow provider to steal five civilian cars left in Be'eri days after the 7 October attacks, bringing his total punishment to 13 years.
A 9-year-old boy in Haifa dies from encephalitis caused by an extremely rare "brain-eating organism" after swimming in the Sea of Galilee.
The IDF states that it detained several civilians attempting to enter into Gaza.
The Supreme Court postpones ruling on the state commission on the 7 October attacks until after the election.

The son of Israeli Ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter is critically injured in a car ramming attack at the Maccabim Junction along Route 443 in the West Bank. The attacker is shot dead at the scene by the IDF.
RealSense, an Israel-based maker of AI vision technology for robots, agrees to sell to Cognex Corporation, an US machine vision maker, for over $600 million.
An Israeli is killed in a gun attack in the vicinity of Halamish, with the Palestinian attacker later caught by the IDF.
President Isaac Herzog pardons a soldier who killed a subdued Palestinian stabber in 2016.
Tel Aviv prohibits sex-segregated selichot services on beaches.
The chief intelligence officer of the Gaza Division during the 7 October attacks is formally dismissed from the IDF.
The Israel Antiquities Authority announces that a 25-ton mikveh from the Second Temple period was discovered in Kiryat Gat.
Thirteen municipalities declare that they will not permit the use of live chickens in the traditional kapparot ritual prior to Yom Kippur.
An Israeli is sentenced to more than 13 years imprisonment for espionage on behalf of Iran.
The renewal of the Israeli government's land registration process in the West Bank, which was halted in 1968 is suspended by the Jerusalem District Court.
Channel 13's sale to a coalition critic is approved by the Second Authority for Television and Radio.
Gate Technologies is acquired by Ondas for up to $390 million.

Israeli and American authorities announce that the IDF chief Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir met with Qatari Armed Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Jassim bin Mohammed bin Ahmed Al Mannai to discuss the Iranian regime despite bilateral tensions between the countries.
Tamar Steinberg wins a gold medal in windsurfing at the iQFoil World Championships.
The IDF announces that a soldier who shot a Palestinian in the West Bank without reason breached rules of engagement.

The Democrats Party leader and former IDF Deputy Chief of Staff Yair Golan announces that he has sued Sara Netanyahu for NIS 2.55 million ($843,000) in defamation and damages after the prime minister's wife implied—without providing proof—that he was able to save lives during the Nova music festival massacre because he had prior knowledge of the 7 October attacks.
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announces that Israel demolished 35 Palestinian structures in the West Bank to make way for new settlement roads.
The Supreme Court overturns the government's appointments to the Second Authority for Television and Radio.
